transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it’s really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of a communication issue at work? It's probably just me being a little too scattered, but... lately, my artist statements and the notes I write up for clients have been kind of all over the place. Like, even when I'm speaking in meetings, I'll start talking about the textures of a piece, and then I guess I just jump straight into the budget, and then suddenly I'm going on about... like, the secret meanings behind the materials. 

People keep telling me they can’t really follow what I’m trying to explain. It's a little embarrassing, honestly, because I really want to come across as professional and put-together. Does that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
Do your thoughts ever feel like they’re moving unusually fast?

Um... maybe a little bit? I mean, I always just assumed it was a normal part of the creative process, but... sometimes, yeah, they do go pretty fast. 

It’s like... before I can even finish thinking through one single idea, everything else just kind of stacks on top of it. Like, I'll have mental images for a piece, and potential titles, and all the formal grant language I need to write, plus colors and bits of conversations... it all just rushes in at the exact same time. 

I try really hard to manage it so I don't seem completely disorganized, though. I really do. Does... does that sound like what you mean by fast? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is around?

Um... well... I guess, sometimes? But it's really nothing scary or anything like that. I don't want you to think I'm, like, completely losing my grip on reality. 

Sometimes when I'm all alone in the studio, working late, I'll hear... like, a woman's voice? Just quietly commenting on things, coming from behind the supply shelves. And sometimes I'll smell this really strong scent of hot metal near a piece I'm working on, even if I haven't been doing any welding or anything. 

It feels completely real in the moment, but then I'll go check behind the shelves or check my equipment, and there's absolutely nothing there. It's probably just my imagination working a little too hard when I'm tired, right? I mean, artists are supposed to have active imaginations... is that something I should be worried about? I hope that doesn't sound too weird...
Have there been times when you heard that voice even when your mood felt completely normal?

Um... yes, actually. I hope it's okay to admit that. I don't want to sound like I'm making a big deal out of it, but... there was this one month recently where things were actually really calm. 

I was sleeping normally, you know? Getting my full eight hours, and I didn't have that... that intense, unstoppable energy I usually get when I'm working on a new series. I felt completely fine, really balanced. But... I was still hearing her. The comments from behind the shelves. And... I was also seeing these little hidden warnings in my studio materials, like the way the clay was drying or how the glaze settled. It went on like that for a few weeks, even though my mood was completely fine. 

Is... is that helpful to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I know it sounds a little strange, but I promise I was feeling totally normal otherwise.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually energized or euphoric for several days in a row?

Um... well, I guess so? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm out of control or anything. I always just thought of it as being really inspired. 

There are these stretches where I just feel... lit up, I guess? Like I'm almost unstoppable and every single idea I have for a piece is just brilliant. It's actually a really great feeling, and I get so much work done. But... I guess there is a downside, too. I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad person, but during those times, if a collaborator or another artist makes even a small comment about my work, I can just... snap. Like, I get really irritable, and my reaction is way bigger than the situation actually calls for. 

I always feel terrible about it afterward. I try really hard to be easy to work with. Does... does that make sense? Is that the kind of energy you're asking about?
During those energized periods, do you need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy?

Um... yeah, actually. I hope that's okay, I know people are supposed to get a lot of sleep. But when I'm in that zone, I really just don't need it. 

I can be in the studio working really late, and then I'll sleep for maybe... two or three hours? And when I wake up, I don't feel groggy or exhausted like I normally would if I pulled a late night. I just feel bright and totally ready to keep going. It's actually really helpful for my art, getting all that extra time. 

I mean, I know it's probably not the healthiest habit long-term, but... it's not super uncommon for artists to have weird schedules when they're inspired, right? I hope that doesn't sound too unhealthy. Is that okay?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I have days where I feel a little down or unmotivated, like anyone else, I think? But... definitely not for two weeks straight, and not most of the day. 

I try really hard to stay positive and keep moving forward, even when things are a little stressful. I don't want to be one of those people who just... wallows, you know? So if I ever feel a bit sad, I usually just push through it and focus on my work. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just... I really haven't had anything like that. Is it okay that I haven't experienced that?
Did the voice and the hidden warnings continue for at least two weeks when your mood felt completely normal?

Um... well, yes. I hope it doesn't sound too strange, but... yeah. 

There was a stretch, maybe a month or so, where things were actually pretty quiet for me. I was sleeping a normal amount again, and I didn't have that... unstoppable feeling I told you about. I was just feeling really even and normal. But... the voice was still there. 

I'd still hear those little comments coming from behind the shelves in the studio. And I was still noticing those hidden warnings in my supplies, just ordinary things like the paint tubes or the canvas wrappers. That went on for a few weeks, even though my mood was totally fine. 

I know it sounds a bit odd to have that happening when I'm otherwise feeling completely normal. I try really hard to just ignore it and focus on the art. Is... is that the kind of thing you're looking for? Does that make sense?
When you hear the woman's voice, does it ever happen only during those high-energy, low-sleep periods?

Um... well, it definitely happens then, too. I hope I'm explaining this right. 

When I'm in those really charged-up periods—when I'm barely sleeping and just taking on way too many projects at once—the voice is definitely there. I'll hear her commenting on things while I'm in the studio. And... that's also when I've felt really sure that the paint stains and the weird phrases in my emails were sending me specific instructions. 

So, yes, it happens during those high-energy times, but like I mentioned before, it also happens when my mood is totally even. I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely losing it when I get inspired, you know? It's just something that kind of overlaps sometimes. Is that okay? Does that answer your question?
Have you had any neurological illness or brain injury?

Um... no, not that I know of. I've never had any kind of brain injury or... or any neurological illness. 

I've always been pretty healthy in that regard. I try to take good care of myself, you know? I haven't been in any bad accidents or hit my head or anything like that. 

I hope that's a good thing? Like, I'm glad I don't have anything like that going on. Is it alright that my answer is no for this one?
During those high-energy periods, do you feel unusually powerful, gifted, or certain that you have special abilities?

Um... well, it's not like I think I have superpowers or anything like that. I really hope it doesn't sound arrogant. I just... I get really confident. 

When I'm at my most charged up, I just feel this... incredible clarity. I truly feel like I'm about to change how everyone understands installation art. It's like I can see exactly how everything needs to come together, and suddenly, normal limits just... don't seem to matter. Things like funding, or time, or even my own experience level—they just don't really apply to me in those moments. I feel like I can accomplish absolutely anything I set my mind to.

I know it probably sounds a bit grand, and I really don't want to come across as conceited. It's just a really intense wave of inspiration. Is it normal for artists to feel that way sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound too out of touch with reality.
Have the voice and the hidden warnings been happening, on and off or continuously, for at least six months?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever, I promise. I really hope it doesn't sound too strange, but... I guess it's been going on for a little while now. 

I'd say the... the messages I see in the materials, and the voice, and sometimes those smells in the studio... it's been about 11 months? Roughly? 

It kind of comes and goes, you know? It's not like it's every single second of every day. I still get a lot of work done, and I function pretty well, I think. I just... I hope 11 months doesn't make it sound too severe. Is that a really long time to be dealing with something like this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
For most of the past 11 months, have the voice and the hidden warnings been present even when you were not in one of those high-energy periods?

Um... well, yes, I guess they have. I really hope that doesn't make things sound worse than they are. 

There was actually a... a quieter month, a little while back? I was sleeping a lot more normally, and I didn't have that huge rush of feeling completely unstoppable. I was just kind of... regular, I guess. But even then, for a few weeks during that time, I still kept hearing those little comments coming from behind the shelves. And I was still noticing those hidden warnings in my ordinary studio materials, like the paint tubes and the canvas grains. 

It wasn't quite as intense as when I'm really charged up, but it was definitely still there. I just... I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the right way.
Over these past 11 months, for most of that time, were the voice and the hidden warnings happening?

Um... well, you know, it hasn't been the *whole* time. I really want to make sure I'm not making it sound like it's this constant, overwhelming thing. 

I guess... well, actually, I'm not entirely sure how to add it all up. It comes and goes, like I said. Sometimes I get really focused on my art and I don't really pay attention to it as much. So, I don't know if I'd say it's been *most* of the time? Maybe? I just haven't really kept a strict log of it, I guess. 

I hope that's an okay answer. I just don't want to exaggerate and make you think I'm doing worse than I actually am, because I really am managing okay. Does that help at all?
Was there ever a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing the voice or noticing the hidden warnings while your mood felt completely normal?

Um... yes, actually. I think I mentioned it just a minute ago, but I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much. 

There was that... that quieter month I brought up? Where my mood was just totally fine, and I wasn't feeling all rushed or unstoppable, and I was sleeping like a normal person. During that time, for, um, I guess a few weeks of it, I was still hearing those little comments from behind the shelves in the studio. And I was still seeing those warnings in my paints and canvases. 

But I promise it didn't completely ruin my days or anything! I was still okay. I just... I hope it's alright that I'm confirming that. Does that give you the information you need?
Looking over the entire 11 months since this started, would you say the voice and hidden warnings were present for more than half of that time?

Um... well, if I really look back at it... I guess, yes. The, um, the messages I see in my materials, and the voice... and sometimes these smells in the studio, too... they really have been happening for roughly the whole 11 months. 

But I promise it's not like it's overwhelming me every single day! It's just sort of there in the background, off and on. I really hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression or making it sound scarier than it actually is, because I'm still getting my work done and taking care of things. I just want to make sure I'm being completely honest with you. Is that... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Over these 11 months, have those high-energy, low-sleep periods taken up most of the time?

Um... well, I guess if I really sit down and look at the whole year... yeah. Those, um, those stretches where I'm just full of energy and getting so much art done, and not really sleeping much... they probably have taken up more of the time than the calmer periods. 

Even though it kind of goes up and down, you know? It's not always at a ten. Sometimes it's just a little bit of extra energy. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm out of control or anything, because I really do try to channel it into my work. It's actually been kind of helpful for my portfolio, if I'm being honest. 

I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. Is it okay that I've had more of those energized days than normal ones? I'm still managing everything, I promise.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or noticing the hidden warnings while your mood felt completely normal?

Um... yes, actually. I know we just touched on this, and I really, really hope I'm not repeating myself too much or wasting your time. 

But, um, yes. There was that quieter month I mentioned, where my mood was just... normal. I was sleeping a regular amount, and I wasn't feeling all rushed or unstoppable like I do when I'm working on a big project. But during that time, for, um, I guess a few weeks of it, I was still hearing those little comments from behind the shelves in the studio. And I was still seeing those warnings in my paints and canvases. 

I just want to be clear, though, it wasn't scary or anything! I was still totally fine and getting by okay. I just... I hope it's alright that I'm bringing it up again. Does that answer what you were asking?
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or noticing the hidden warnings while your mood felt completely normal?

Um... I think we might have just talked about that, actually. I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before, I really don't want to make things confusing for you. 

But yes, there was that one quieter month I brought up just a minute ago. My mood was completely fine, you know? I was sleeping normally, and I wasn't having those big bursts of energy where I feel like I can do anything. But even though I felt totally calm and normal, for a few weeks during that time, I was still hearing those little comments coming from behind the studio shelves. And I was still noticing those warnings in my materials. 

I really hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need. Does that make sense, or did you need me to explain it differently?
Over the whole 11 months since this began, have the energized or irritable periods been present for most of that time?

Um... I know we kind of touched on this a little bit already, and I'm so sorry if I'm making you ask things twice. I really want to be helpful and give you the right information. 

But, um, yes. If I really look back over the whole 11 months since this all started... those stretches where I'm super energized, maybe a little irritable, and just getting so much work done... they definitely have taken up more of the year than the calmer times. 

It's not always super intense, though! It definitely rises and falls, and sometimes it's just a really productive week where I'm just very focused on my art. I hope that's okay, that I've been like that for most of the year. I really do try to make the most of it and channel it into my portfolio. Does that answer your question alright?
